title: Give every wagon produce/consume entry a version-free contract URN that resolves in the registry

facts.note: Alternatives (OR): a wagon manifest under plan/{wagon}/ OR the contract registry. Either path alone activates; an ordinary manifest edit does not require the registry to be touched too.
Authoring a new wagon, editing a manifest, rolling URNs out across manifests, or editing registry ids/producer fields.

values: registry contract id or producer field added/changed/removed
facts.note: Needs a YAML-diff observer over manifests (produce/consume entries, urn fields) and over the registry (id, producer). A pure version bump that keeps the id prefix and producer is excluded.
Covers the URN rollout/upgrade task across all wagon artifacts.

fires: Planner adds a produce entry to a new wagon manifest under plan/{wagon}/
Planner adds a consume entry referencing an artifact produced by another wagon
Planner edits an existing urn field or renames a produced/consumed artifact
Planner meets a legacy dot-for-hierarchy URN such as contract:{domain}.{resource} in a manifest
Planner runs the URN upgrade: adding urn to all wagon artifacts, validating resolution, generating contracts for orphaned URNs
Planner changes a contract id or producer field in contracts/_artifacts.yaml so a wagon URN may no longer resolve or link back
doesNotFire: Editing prose docs or acceptances that do not touch wagon manifest produce/consume entries or registry ids/producers
Bumping a contract version in contracts/_artifacts.yaml (e.g. :v1 -> :v2) without renaming the artifact or changing its producer (URN stays unchanged)
Code-only changes outside plan/ and contracts/

given: A wagon manifest (plan/{wagon}/*.yaml) has produce/consume entries naming artifacts {domain}:{resource}[.{category}], linked to contracts/_artifacts.yaml.
when: You author/edit those entries, roll URNs out across wagons, or change registry ids or producers.
then: Each produce/consume entry carries `urn: contract:{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]` (no version) that resolves to a registry id {same}:v{N} whose producer names the producing wagon.
prefer: Derive from the name: domain before the first colon, resource up to an optional dot, category after it; mechanic:decision.choice -> contract:mechanic:decision.choice.
Same URN on the producer's produce entry and every consume entry (consume names `from wagon:<producer>`).
Upgrade in order: add urn to all wagon artifacts; validate all resolve; generate missing contracts for orphaned URNs.
avoid: Legacy dot hierarchy contract:mechanic.decision.choice; migrate it.
Versions (:v1) or schema/API detail in the URN.
Changing URNs when a contract moves v1->v2.
unless: Pre-URN wagons: urn is optional initially; required for new wagons.
why: Wagons declare WHAT (URN), contracts HOW (version, schema, API): contracts evolve without wagon YAML changes, names stay readable, and the graph keeps bidirectional wagon<->contract linkage.
evidence: Every produce/consume entry in plan/{wagon}/*.yaml has an urn matching ^contract:[^:.]+:[^:.]+(\.[^:.]+)?$ and equal to 'contract:' + the entry name.
Each URN resolves to a contract in the registry (contracts/_artifacts.yaml): some id {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]:v* matches.
The matched contract's producer field resolves back to the wagon whose produce entry carries the URN (bidirectional linkage).

Positive: maintain-ux produce name ux:foundations, urn contract:ux:foundations, to external; maintain-ux produce name ux:foundations.colors, urn contract:ux:foundations.colors, to external; stage-characters consume name ux:foundations, urn contract:ux:foundations, from wagon:maintain-ux.
verifier_detail: URN format: contract:{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]. domain = artifact-name part before the first colon; resource = after the first colon, before the dot if present; category = optional part after the dot. Conversion rule: keep colon for hierarchy, preserve category as dot facet.

Name->URN examples: ux:foundations -> contract:ux:foundations; ux:foundations.colors -> contract:ux:foundations.colors; mechanic:decision.choice -> contract:mechanic:decision.choice; match:result -> contract:match:result; player:identity -> contract:player:identity.

Contract id field in contracts/_artifacts.yaml: id: {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]:v{version}; authoritative for schema, version, API. URN contract:{domain}:{resource}[.{category}] maps to any version of id {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]:v*.

Id matching examples: id ux:foundations:v1 (version 1.0.0, path ux/foundations.json, producer wagon:maintain-ux) matches urn contract:ux:foundations; id ux:foundations.colors:v1 matches urn contract:ux:foundations.colors (category preserved in both URN and ID).
Linkage: wagon URN -> contract id lookup via domain.resource matching; contract producer field -> wagon name. Validation: URN must resolve to a contract in the registry.

Legacy normalisation: contract:{domain}.{resource} -> contract:{domain}:{resource}; category stays as a dot facet contract:{domain}:{resource}.{category}. Counter-example: contract:mechanic.decision.choice -> contract:mechanic:decision.choice.
Backward compatibility: missing urn on pre-existing wagons tolerated initially; missing urn on new wagons is a finding.
Rollout phases: phase1 add urn field to all wagon artifacts (this upgrade); phase2 validate all URNs resolve to contracts; phase3 generate missing contracts for orphaned URNs.

additions.text: The statement's two halves (well-formed version-free URN; graph-maintained bidirectional linkage / registry resolution) are kept together in then as one obligation: a correctly formed URN that resolves and links back. No split; the source makes resolution mandatory ('A URN must resolve to a contract in the registry').
additions.justification: Auditor required resolution/linkage as an active obligation, not prefer/evidence only.

additions.text: Regex ^contract:[^:.]+:[^:.]+(\.[^:.]+)?$ and the 'contract:' + name equality check.
additions.justification: Mechanical restatement of the source format/derivation for verifiers; not a new obligation.
